                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>
                                             </div>

About the Role <\/strong><\/h2>

We are looking for a Customer Success Manager to own the relationship with the customers connected to our out\u2011of\u2011home (OOH) delivery platform. <\/p>

You will be the first contact for our customers. You know their numbers, and when a customer is stuck, you are the one who gets things moving inside GLS\/NXT. You work at the intersection of product, engineering, data and commercial, and you are measured on customer outcomes rather than on activity. <\/p>

This role is perfect for someone who likes owning results across organisational boundaries, is comfortable with data, and can hold their own with a customer's operations director in the morning and our engineering leads in the afternoon. <\/p>

What you will do <\/strong><\/p>

  • Own customer relationships: <\/strong>Act as the main contact for connected customers across markets, from onboarding through to steady\u2011state growth <\/p><\/li>

  • Drive customer performance: <\/strong>Own adoption and performance KPIs per customer, such as platform utilisation and integration health, and deliver measurable improvement Resolve blockers: Spot what is holding customers back and bring in the right GLS\/NXT teams to solve it <\/p><\/li>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              About Nous<\/strong><\/h2>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              And it's working. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of \"to do great work with really smart people\".<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          About Nous<\/strong><\/h2>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of \"to do great work with really smart people\".<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          \u00a0<\/div>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          How we build (worth reading before the role)<\/strong><\/h2>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          \u00a0<\/div>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          About the role<\/strong><\/h2>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you\u2019d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          You\u2019ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          That's also what makes it exciting.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren\u2019t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what\u2019s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad\u2019s energy up. You won\u2019t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won\u2019t be just another builder in the squad either: when you\u2019re heads-down building, you can\u2019t unblock anyone or bring the team together.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we\u2019re particularly interested in PMs who\u2019ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as \"product\".<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          We need all of these at once:<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up.<\/p><\/li>

Wir bei Insurgo

Wir bei Insurgo sind nicht nur ein Technologie-Unternehmen. Wir sind Innovatoren, die den Weg für digitale Lösungen in der Versicherungswirtschaft ebnen. Hunderte Maklerbüros arbeiten bereits mit unserer Software, unser Postfach Plus nimmt ihnen bis zu 80 Prozent ihres Verwaltungsaufwands ab, und unsere Kunden bewerten uns über 900 Mal.

Wir entwickeln Insurgo zunehmend mit KI-Agenten. Nicht als Spielerei und nicht im Blindflug: Agenten übernehmen einen wachsenden Teil der Umsetzung, du gibst die Richtung vor, prüfst, entscheidest und verantwortest das Ergebnis. Genau dafür suchen wir dich.

Aufgaben

Als Senior Software Engineer entwickelst du unsere Plattform in voller Breite weiter. Du arbeitest fachlich eng mit unserem Product Management zusammen und berichtest an den Geschäftsführer.

  • Plattform weiterentwickeln: Du verantwortest Features vom Rails-Backend über die REST-API bis ins Angular-Frontend, von der Idee bis zum Release.
  • Agentic Engineering: Du arbeitest täglich mit Coding-Agenten wie Cursor, Claude Code und GitHub Copilot. Du zerlegst Aufgaben so, dass Agenten sie zuverlässig umsetzen, und sicherst die Qualität über Code Review und Tests.
  • Wissen für Mensch und Agent: Du baust mit uns eine lebende Wissensbasis über Code, Architektur und Fachlichkeit auf, mit der Entwickler und Agenten gleichermaßen arbeiten können.
  • KI im Produkt: Du entwickelst unseren Insurgo Agent und weitere KI-Funktionen weiter, die Maklern spürbar Arbeit abnehmen.
  • Integrationen: Du kümmerst dich um Branchenschnittstellen wie BiPRO und VEMA, E-Mail-Anbindungen, digitale Post und elektronische Signatur.
  • Stabiler Betrieb: Wir releasen täglich. Du sorgst mit dafür, dass unsere Plattform dabei sicher, schnell und verlässlich läuft.

Womit du arbeitest

  • Mandantenfähige SaaS-Plattform, jeder Mandant mit eigenem Datenbankschema
  • Backend: Ruby on Rails, Sidekiq, Action Cable
  • Frontend: Angular mit TypeScript
  • API: REST/JSON mit OpenAPI und Webhooks, genutzt von unserem Frontend, von Kunden und von Automationen wie Zapier
  • Mobile: zwei Flutter-Apps für iOS und Android
  • Daten: PostgreSQL, Redis, S3
  • Add-ons: Gmail, Outlook, WhatsApp Web, Thunderbird und Missive
  • Hosting: AWS in Frankfurt, hochverfügbar und DSGVO-konform
  • Arbeitsweise: Kanban in Jira, Pull Requests und Code Review in Bitbucket, tägliche Releases auf Staging und Production

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit:

  • Senior-Erfahrung: Du hast mehrere Jahre professionell Webanwendungen entwickelt und Verantwortung für Systeme im Produktivbetrieb getragen.
  • Architektur und Systemdesign: Du denkst in Systemen, nicht in einzelnen Codezeilen. Mandantenfähige SaaS, saubere APIs, Datenmodelle und Hintergrundverarbeitung entwirfst du so, dass sie langfristig tragen.
  • Requirements Engineering: Du übersetzt fachliche Anforderungen in klare, umsetzbare Spezifikationen, für Menschen genauso wie für Agenten.
  • Agentisches Entwickeln: Du hast verstanden, wie man mit Coding-Agenten gute Software baut. Vor allem kannst du der KI den passenden Kontext liefern, damit sie gute Ergebnisse erzeugt, und willst damit moderne Lösungen entwickeln.
  • Code verstehen und bewerten: Du musst nicht jede Zeile selbst schreiben, aber du verstehst KI-generierten Code in Ruby on Rails und Angular mit TypeScript und kannst seine Qualität sicher beurteilen.
  • Eigenständigkeit: Du arbeitest selbstorganisiert und pragmatisch, triffst Entscheidungen und gehst auch mal neue Wege, statt auf Aufgaben zu warten.
  • Fließendes Deutsch: Du stimmst dich täglich mit Product Management und Support ab und verstehst die Fachlichkeit unserer Kunden.
  • Starker Pluspunkt: Erfahrung in der Versicherungsbranche, idealerweise im Maklerumfeld oder mit Schnittstellen wie BiPRO.
  • Pluspunkt: Erfahrung mit Flutter, AWS-Betrieb oder Integrationen wie Office-Add-ins und Browser-Extensions.

Benefits

  • Ein ambitioniertes Team aus A-Playern
  • Moderner Arbeitsplatz mit Top-Ausstattung
  • Kompetitives Gehalt
  • Offene Kommunikation und ergebnisorientiertes Arbeiten
  • 100€ Arbeitgeberfinanzierte Altersversorgung
  • 50€ Gutscheinkarte jeden Monat, steuerfrei zur freien Verfügung
  • Teamevents, die in Erinnerung bleiben
  • Sicherer und unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag

Voraussetzung für diese Position ist ein Wohnsitz in Deutschland sowie eine bestehende Arbeitserlaubnis.

Bewerbung

Klingt interessant? Dann freuen wir uns auf Deine Bewerbung! Im Bewerbungsprozess erwartet Dich ein praxisnahes Assessment, bei dem Du zeigst, wie Du mit KI-Agenten entwickelst. Bitte vergiss nicht, Deine Gehaltsvorstellung und Deinen frühestmöglichen Starttermin anzugeben.

Senior Software-Entwickler (m/w/d) – PHP/Symfony & React – Berlin

Der Plan steht, jetzt fehlst du: Bring unsere Software von Legacy-PHP auf Symfony und React.

Auf einen Blick

  • Stack: PHP 8.1 (Legacy) → Symfony · jQuery/Vanilla-JS → React · MySQL/MariaDB, SingleStore · Git, CI/CD

Die Rolle

Unser Kernprodukt Konsentas ist über viele Jahre gewachsen, und das sieht man dem Code an. Das Backend läuft auf PHP 8.1 ohne Framework. Im Frontend stehen jQuery und Vanilla-JS neben React, und automatisierte Tests gibt es bisher wenige.

Wohin es gehen soll, ist klar: Das Backend wird schrittweise auf Symfony umgestellt, das Frontend auf React vereinheitlicht. Bis Ende 2027 soll die Migration abgeschlossen sein. Was dafür fehlt, ist kein Plan, sondern Kapazität.

Du triffst eigenständig technische Entscheidungen, bringst dich in Architektur- und Modernisierungsfragen ein und sorgst dafür, dass die Codequalität mit jedem Release besser wird. Dabei bleibt das Produkt im Einsatz: Wartung, Support und neue Features laufen parallel zur Modernisierung.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Legacy-Module bei laufendem Betrieb schrittweise durch Symfony-Services und React-Oberflächen ersetzen

  • Fullstack-Features von der Datenbank bis zum Frontend entwickeln, teils auch als kundenspezifische Erweiterungen

  • Bestehenden Legacy-Code pflegen, debuggen und weiterentwickeln

  • Code-Reviews durchführen und die Testabdeckung ausbauen

  • Mit Entwicklungsleitung und Geschäftsführung abstimmen, welche Bereiche als Nächstes modernisiert werden

  • Unsere zwei Auszubildenden im letzten Ausbildungsabschnitt fachlich begleiten (ohne disziplinarische Führung)

  • Gelegentlich an Kundenterminen teilnehmen, etwa alle 3–4 Wochen

Nach 6 Monaten …

… setzt du Features eigenständig um, hast spürbar zur Modernisierung beigetragen, die Codequalität verbessert und bist für unsere Azubis eine feste Ansprechperson.

Dein Profil

  • Erfahrung: etwa 4–5 Jahre in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung (ein Richtwert, keine harte Grenze)

  • PHP: fundierte Kenntnisse in modernem PHP 8.x mit objektorientierter Architektur, etwa Dependency Injection, Interfaces und SOLID

  • Symfony: nachweisbare Praxiserfahrung mit dem Framework

  • Legacy-Code: Du gehst sicher mit gewachsenen Codebasen um. Du refaktorierst, debuggst und entwickelst weiter, ohne alles neu zu schreiben.

  • JavaScript/React: solide Erfahrung im Frontend, jQuery schreckt dich nicht ab

  • Datenbanken: relationale Datenbanken wie MySQL/MariaDB oder SingleStore und sicherer Umgang mit SQL

  • Tooling: Git und Arbeit mit CI/CD

  • Sprache: Deutsch auf C1-Niveau, Englisch mindestens B1

  • Arbeitsweise: eigenständig, strukturiert, proaktiv und mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch

  • Persönlich: Du kommunizierst verlässlich, arbeitest gern im Team, übernimmst Verantwortung, hast keine Angst vor schwierigen Codestellen und gibst dein Wissen gern weiter.

  • Abschluss: Ausbildung oder FH-Abschluss zählen bei uns genauso viel wie ein Uni-Studium. Entscheidend ist deine Praxiserfahrung.

Pluspunkte: REST/API-Design und Schnittstellenentwicklung, automatisiertes Testing (PHPUnit, Jest), Docker, Deployment-Pipelines und Cloud, Software-Architektur und Design

Patterns, produktiver Einsatz von KI-Tools wie Claude Code oder Codex. Erfahrung mit Software für den öffentlichen Sektor ist nicht nötig.

Ein kleines Team mit kurzen Wegen: Daniel (Developer Lead), Nico (Geschäftsführer & Projektmanager), der selbst aktiv mitentwickelt, ein externer Entwickler und zwei Auszubildende. Ihr stimmt euch täglich ab. Daniel und Nico übernehmen dein Onboarding persönlich.

  3. Teamgespräch vor Ort

  4. Angebot

Über Girona

Seit über 25 Jahren entwickelt die Girona Softwareentwicklung GmbH in Berlin Software für die öffentliche Verwaltung. Städte wie Berlin, München, Bonn und Dessau setzen seit Jahrzehnten auf unsere Lösungen, Konsentas etwa in Bürgerämtern, Gesundheitsämtern sowie Kfz-Zulassungs- und Führerscheinstellen.

    • Ensure G2's internal teams understand the value each partner brings and how to activate them to drive revenue for their own books of business.

    • Build rapport with sales and partners as an expert on G2 and our partner ecosystem

    • Create leverage on the Partnership team by consistently sharing new learnings and industry insights

    We are looking for a Senior Partner Deployed Engineer to join the Customer Solutions team, focused on building Coder’s partner ecosystem across EMEA.     This is not a support role. You are equally comfortable holding a strategic roadmap conversation with a partner CTO and debugging a Kubernetes deployment in a partner’s lab in the same afternoon.     • Serve as the strategic technical thought partner to EMEA partner leadership, including practice leads, CTOs, and solutions architects at global systems integrators, regional cloud consultancies, and hyperscaler field teams. Own the technical relationship and set the vision for how Coder fits into each partner’s AI and modernization portfolio.

    • Co-create sales plays tailored to each partner’s customer base, vertical focus, and services capabilities. Author Working Backwards outcome proposals for strategic partner-customer combinations that translate AI Development Infrastructure into deal-level urgency.

    • Intervene directly on the highest-value partner-attached deals across EMEA: co-sell calls, technical discovery, PoV scoping, architecture review, and technical win support. Own the engagement until the partner’s team can carry it independently.

    • Produce “better together” reference architectures for strategic partner combinations across cloud providers and AI platforms. Include deployment diagrams, network topology, IAM patterns, and operational runbooks that partner SAs can hand directly to customers.

    • Build AI-powered self-service tools that automate high-volume PDE activities: Opportunity Brief Generator, PR/FAQ Generator, Workshop-in-a-Box deployment, and demo site builder.

    Help us make a big green dent in the universe. We're on a mission to drive the global renewable energy revolution, and we need many more people to help us make our vision a reality.
     
    Octopus Energy Generation (OEGEN) is a leader in sourcing, investing in, and managing a wide range of utility-scale renewable energy assets. As we continue to expand our investment base, we are dedicated to building a diverse team that reflects the communities we serve. Currently, we manage a global portfolio of over £8 billion in renewable energy assets.
     
    We are committed to delivering best-in-class responsible investment activity, offering like-minded investors the means and products to invest their capital sustainably. It is our ambition to change the entire energy lifecycle and make every green electron matter, delivering the best outcomes for customers, investors, the environment and society, accelerating the transition to net zero.

    OEGEN Data, Tech & Transformation Team 

    We are embarking on a comprehensive transformation program designed to drive significant advancements in our business operations and technology landscape. Our primary goal is to transition from our current reliance on legacy systems and specialized off-the-shelf tools to a more integrated, AI-driven, and data-centric operational model. 

    Leveraging insights and guidance from our other technically mature entities like Kraken and OE, we plan to adopt cutting-edge tools and capabilities, particularly in AI and Python-driven solutions. 

    By investing in a diverse range of skills, we aim to create a hybrid team capable of operating in both our legacy and future environments, ultimately transforming OEGEN into an efficient, data-driven organization.

    About the role

    We’re looking for a Data Engineer who can own the journey of data from source systems to decision-ready outputs. You’ll build and maintain pipelines, model data, stand up dashboards, and integrate systems via APIs. In a team this size, you’ll also get involved in application development - building internal tools with Streamlit, FastAPI, or HTMX that put data directly in the hands of our investment and asset management teams. 

    In your first 3 months you’ll have taken ownership of at least one critical pipeline from an external system into Databricks, and built or materially improved a reporting layer used by Fund Management or Asset Management. 


    What you'll do
  • Design, build, and maintain scalable data pipelines in Databricks, ensuring data is reliable, timely, and well-documented.
  • Own and evolve our Databricks models - define schemas, enforce testing, and keep the warehouse clean.
  • Automate manual data processes using Python, replacing spreadsheets and ad-hoc workflows with robust, repeatable jobs.
  • Build performance dashboards and reports in Streamlit and HTMX (FastAPI) that Finance, Asset Management, and Fund Management actually use.
  • Integrate internal and third-party systems via REST APIs, improving data accessibility across the business.
  • Champion data quality - implement validation, monitoring, and governance practices that give stakeholders confidence in the numbers.
  • Collaborate directly with non-technical teams to understand their problems and translate them into data solutions. 

    • What you'll need
  • Strong SQL and Python skills, used daily for pipeline development, data modelling, and automation.
  • Experience with modern data stack tooling: a cloud data platform (Databricks preferred), and version control (Git/GitHub).
  • A solid understanding of data modelling, warehousing patterns, and ETL/ELT design.
  • To be comfortable working with Postgres or similar relational databases.
  • Clear communication - you can explain a data model to a fund manager and discuss trade-offs with an engineer.
  • A bias toward shipping: you’d rather get something working and iterate than spend weeks in design. 

    • Bonus points for
  • Full-stack development experience - particularly with Streamlit, FastAPI, or HTMX.
  • Experience building and managing REST APIs, including authentication, rate limiting, and documentation.
  • Familiarity with renewable energy, infrastructure investment, or financial services data.
  • Experience evaluating and adopting AI/ML tooling to augment engineering workflows.

    The team

    The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and Customer Lifetime Value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy.

    The team is around twelve data scientists. Some work on auto-space models that decide within five minutes from data candidates authorise us to pull. Others work on manual-space models that pick up when a credit analyst adds digital footprint and income data, which lands a decision within 24 hours.

    • Causal estimation of offer terms. Modelling how amount, duration, and price shape customer outcomes.

    • Unifying auto and manual models. The two families were built without forced technical alignment. Finding a principled way to unify them on a common cost function is open work.

    • IFRS accounting model. A multi-stage credit model where information propagates back from later-stage recovery predictions to sharpen upfront loss estimates.

    • Generalising credit and CLtV. Whether a more general framing could replace both separate models is an open research question.

    • Domain experience. You have worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling.

    • Non-linear methods. You have shipped gradient boosting or neural networks on tabular data in production.

    • Bayesian methods. You have used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work.

    • Time series modelling. You have modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered.

    • Python. The stack the team uses.

    We expect to pay from £90,000 – £120,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

    Agentic AI for Semi-Automating the Data Science Workflow 

    Ekimetrics is the European leader in data science, with over 500 data scientists and 1,000+ projects since 2006.     Within Ekimetrics, the Innovation Department works on AI research topics in collaboration with our industrial and academic partners. The department comprises several PhD experts in generative AI, deep learning, computer vision, time series, explainability, and causality. Each expert leads teams tasked with studying and building state-of-the-art methods and adapting them to specific business problems, developing new methodologies or algorithms to address identified challenges, and ensuring a seamless handover for integration within Ekimetrics' industrial ecosystem. 

    A central focus of the Innovation Department is closing the gap between cutting-edge AI agents and the day-to-day reality of delivering data science at scale. The department is investing in agentic systems that accelerate the data science lifecycle while keeping data scientists firmly in control of quality, governance, and business relevance. This internship sits at the heart of that effort, combining applied AI research with production-grade engineering on Ekimetrics' modern data stack. 

    Internship Objective: From a Business Question to a Trusted Recommendation 

    LLM-based agents have made rapid progress in the past two years: they can now write, run and tune machine learning code with little human help. Yet real data science projects rarely start from a clean, well-defined task. They start from a business question and imperfect data, and the early choices (what to predict, how to measure success, how to validate) decide whether the result can be trusted. Automating these steps calls for assistants that know when to ask, when to stop, and how to back every claim with evidence. 

    The Innovation Department is building remit, a harness that semi-automates the data science workflow. At each step of a project (framing, data design, exploratory analysis, modeling, evaluation), AI agents draft the output, automatic checks catch common mistakes such as data leakage, and a data scientist reviews and accepts the result before moving on. Ultimately, a business user brings a question and a dataset, and the system frames the problem, prepares and explores the data, compares models against a simple baseline, and returns a clear recommendation in which every figure can be traced back to the data. 

    The work builds on recent research in agentic data science [1]. Agents now earn medals on many of the Kaggle competitions in MLE-bench [2], yet they tend to guess silently rather than ask when a task is ambiguous [3]. Meanwhile, tabular foundation models such as TabICLv2 [4] give strong predictive models without any tuning. 

    The intern will work with senior data scientists and AI builders to build and refine remit. This internship offers an opportunity to engage with cutting-edge AI research and production engineering. 

    Key Responsibilities 

    The intern will: 

    • Review the latest research on agentic data science and on the evaluation of AI agents, building on the team's recent review. 

    • Design and implement remit's agents, starting with problem framing and data design, together with the automatic checks that catch mistakes such as data leakage. 

    • Help define how the system works with business users: when to ask a clarifying question, when to stop rather than guess, and how to explain results in plain language. 

    • Extend the system toward modeling and evaluation, building on trusted tools (scikit-learn, AutoML, tabular foundation models) rather than free-form generated code. 

    • Build a benchmark of realistic business cases, run experiments to measure quality, reliability and cost, and take part in a pilot with business users. 

    • Help integrate the system with the Databricks stack (Unity Catalog, MLflow) and support the safe and governed operation of the agents.

    • Good grasp of model validation: train/test splits, data leakage, baselines.

    • Familiarity with large language models and agentic techniques (prompting, tool calling, structured outputs, evaluation). 

    • Strong Python skills and a solid command of the standard data science toolkit (pandas/polars, scikit-learn, gradient-boosting libraries). 

    • Fluency in English. 

    • Nice to have: experience with an agent framework, solid software engineering practices (git, code review, testing), and exposure to Databricks, MLflow or cloud data platforms.

    Internship Objective: From Latent Reasoning to Better and More Understandable Tabular Models 

     

    Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) such as TabPFN, TabICL or TabDPT are transformers pre-trained on large collections of mostly synthetic datasets. They learn in context: the training data and the points to predict are given as input, and predictions come out of a single forward pass, with no dataset-specific training or tuning. They now rival gradient boosting on many benchmarks [3], which is changing how tabular modeling is practiced. 

    In large language models, a growing line of research lets the model “reason” in its latent space rather than through generated tokens, using extra depth-wise computation, reused continuous hidden states or internal iterations. This latent reasoning can improve performance without longer text outputs [1, 2]. Our hypothesis is that a similar mechanism can improve TFMs: spending more latent compute at inference on hard or ambiguous cases could help them make better use of the in-context examples. Almost all existing work on latent reasoning targets natural language, and its transfer to tabular models, whose architecture, pre-training data and output differ profoundly, remains largely unexplored. 

    Mechanistic interpretability is starting to open the black box, both for latent-reasoning language models and for TFMs themselves [4]. It lets us ask not only whether latent reasoning improves a TFM, but also what the model actually computes during these extra steps, and whether that computation is faithful and useful. The internship therefore has two goals: designing and evaluating latent reasoning mechanisms for TFMs, and using interpretability methods to analyze what they learn. 

    The intern will work with senior researchers and data scientists. This internship offers an opportunity to contribute to an emerging research topic at the intersection of tabular modeling, latent reasoning and interpretability.

    • Identify and adapt latent reasoning mechanisms to TFM architectures (e.g. iterative depth-wise computation, hidden-state reuse). 

    • Implement them on open-source TFMs and measure their effect on accuracy, calibration and robustness against strong baselines (gradient boosting, standard TFMs) at comparable compute. 

    • Apply interpretability methods (representation analysis, probing, activation patching) to characterize the computation performed during latent reasoning. 

    • Build an evaluation protocol on diverse tabular datasets, including realistic business cases. 

    • Document the results and contribute to scientific publications.

    Exeon is a Swiss cyber security company based in Zurich.     • Strong programming skills in Python and Bash (or comparable languages), with a focus on automation and maintainable, production-quality code

    • Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
